chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: The gangsters wreck a rival Harlem club
summary: A would-be rival club on 125th Street that ignored the Cotton Club's warning is vandalized overnight, so the show never opens.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Let's talk about the Cotton Club downtown, Foots.

See, the Cotton Club wanted to move downtown, but for some reason or another they couldn't move down there. So eventually, they worked out a deal... We found out... See, they did it right. Because we was foolin' around with another guy, with some clubs in New York. And they told this guy "Don't open up a club in Harlem." He was going to call it The Plantation or something. And the Cotton Club told him "Don't open no club in Harlem." So he

went ahead. He was bullheaded. He got this club on 125th Street, and decorated, boy, they had a ceiling that would open up so you could see the sky and all that. And we went in and rehearsed the show that day, and we was goin' to come back that night and do the show.

When we come back that night to do the show, somebody had come in there and chopped up the dance floor, cut the strings on the piano... Now, how they knew between the show music and our music, I'll never know. Tore the show music in half. Didn't scratch an instrument of ours and didn't scratch a piece of our arrangement -- none of the things in our book that was (?). And how they knew all that.... And we knew who did it. It never did come out. But they told the man not to open up, but he was bullheaded and... We didn't open either.
